text: The completeness theorem for propositional logic states that if φ is a tautology (⊨ φ) then φ is derivable (⊢ φ); combined with soundness, this yields ⊨ φ if and only if ⊢ φ.
explanation: True. Completeness is ⊨ ⟹ ⊢, and soundness is the converse ⊢ ⟹ ⊨, so together they give the equivalence ⊨ φ ↔ ⊢ φ. The chapter proves completeness via the Lindenbaum–Tarski construction (every consistent set is satisfiable).
